analyticalQuestion: Does amplitude doping in the exact unforced 2.5D recurrence family make a prescribed target-shell atom outgrow the complete normalized Leray-rotational ledger, and does the finite nonlinear Fourier-coset calculation follow the predicted powers?
takeaway: The certified leading ledger has atom-to-complete-ledger proxy order q^1 for alpha=3/2. Independently, the retained-coset nonlinear calculation has atom-proxy order q^1, rotational-charge order q^-1, a stable normalized second-root slope, and truncation agreement at q=1024.
nonColorEncoding: filled circles versus open squares and diamonds

panels.A: certified leading atom divided by the complete-ledger proxy over the asymptotic q sweep
panels.B: nonlinear retained-coset atom proxy and full retained H^-1 rotational charge
panels.C: normalized second-root slope and q=1024 truncation-radius audit

claimBoundary: Panel A is extracted from the exact/high-precision R0.71W certificate and its independent reconstruction. Panels B and C are a finite retained Fourier-coset DOP853 plus nonlinear least-squares corroboration. The retained-coset calculation includes every retained convolution mode and a stated time-tail upper bound. It is not DNS, does not prove spectral-truncation convergence or the uniform continuum implicit-function theorem, and does not prove any Navier-Stokes regularity claim. The amplitude-doped data have unbounded initial energy and enstrophy, so the result tests a data-uniform ledger only.
